newsitem.title: USA: Texas doctor sues Merck in patent dispute.
newsitem.headline: Texas doctor sues Merck in patent dispute.

text.p: A Texas physician on Tuesday filed a civil lawsuit against Merck & Co Inc., seeking $3.75 billion in alleged damages and claiming the U.S. pharmaceuticals giant stole his invention to treat eye disease.

The lawsuit, filed on behalf of William Eric Sponsel, chief of glaucoma service at the University of Texas Health Science Center at San Antonio, alleged Merck "secretly filed patent applications stealing Sponsel's inventions" after Sponsel "confidentially disclosed his inventions to Merck" in 1995 and 1996.
A Merck spokeswoman declined comment on the suit. "As a matter of policy, Merck never comments on pending litigation," Carol Goodrich, spokeswoman for the Whitehouse Station, N.J. company said.

Sponsel's lawsuit, filed in a state district court in San Antonio, said Sponsel had discovered that Carbonic Anhydrase Inhibitors, or CAI, would be useful in treating certain ocular diseases by increasing blood flow velocity in the retina, and that diseases such as macular edema and macular degeneration could be successfully treated by applying CAI topically.

Sponsel's attorney, Raul M. Rodriguez of San Antonio, said in a statement issued after the lawsuit was filed that Sponsel discovered that Trusopt, a drug produced and trademarked by Merck based on the disputed patent approval, can be used topically. The lawsuit said that Merck received patents for the drug as the "assignee of the invention when, in fact, Dr. Sponsel has never assigned the invention to Merck."
"This is one of the biggest breakthroughs in eye treatment this century, and Merck has utterly failed to acknowledge Dr. Sponsel's contribution," Rodriguez said.
Rodriguez said Sponsel indicated the any proceeds from the lawsuit would be used for medical research.
